facts.text: Ashland was named after Henry Clay’s estate, Ashland, reflecting the town’s early ties to American political heritage.
Founded in 1870, Ashland grew around a limestone ledge that made Salt Creek a natural ford for westward travelers.
The Ashland History Museum, housed in a former Carnegie Library, showcases artifacts and photographs dating back to the town’s 1870 founding.
A variant of the Oregon Trail, the Oxbow Trail ran from Nebraska City to Fort Kearny, passing through Ashland’s historic corridor.
Ashland’s historic downtown hosts local wineries like Cellar 426 and Glacial Till Cider House, offering regional craft beverages.
The Ashland History Museum also displays historic aircraft, missiles, and space vehicles, adding a unique aerospace collection.
